title: McDonald confronts Hynek over the swamp gas explanation

tellings.quote: goes to and he's a serious physicist. He goes to J. Allen Hynek and he says, "You've been, you know, taking part in this cover-up. This is ridiculous. Like, what you saw in Michigan wasn't swamp gas.

tellings.link_reason: McDonald angrily confronting Hynek about what he did to science matches the existing confrontation story.

plain: In the 1960s, the story goes, a physicist named James McDonald went to the astronomer J. Allen Hynek and angrily told him he was taking part in a cover-up of UFO sightings. Michels tells it himself, without naming a source. In his version, McDonald, whom he calls a serious physicist, tells Hynek that what people saw in Michigan was not swamp gas, which was the explanation Hynek had given for a wave of sightings there. A researcher who goes by RedPandaKoala tells it too, also without a source, and says McDonald was furious and told Hynek that what he was doing to science was horrible. In RedPandaKoala's version, this confrontation is a big part of why Hynek later changed his stance and came clean about UFOs.
